channel.title: Legacy Medical Journal
channel.description: Health notes from Legacy Medical, a concierge internal medicine practice in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida.

item.title: Can you pay concierge fees from an HSA or FSA?
item.description: A 2026 IRS rule lets HSAs pay some direct primary care fees. Why concierge fees may not qualify, how FSAs differ, and why to ask a tax advisor first.

item.title: Does Medicare cover concierge medicine?
item.description: Medicare does not pay concierge membership fees, but it still covers your visits and tests. Here is how assignment works and what gets billed to Medicare.

item.title: Concierge medicine and direct primary care are not the same
item.description: Concierge medicine and direct primary care both charge a membership, but they differ on insurance billing, fee structure, Florida law and the new HSA rule.

item.title: Concierge medicine vs. MDVIP: how the models differ
item.description: How a national affiliate network like MDVIP differs from an independent concierge practice, and the questions worth asking before you join either one.

item.title: How much does concierge medicine cost?
item.description: What shapes a concierge medicine fee, what a 2005 federal report found, why insurance is still billed for visits, and the questions to ask before you join.

item.title: 12 questions to ask at a concierge meet and greet
item.description: A practical checklist for your first meeting with a concierge doctor: what to ask about access, fees, insurance, hospitals, family updates and records.

item.title: How to choose a concierge doctor in Palm Beach County
item.description: How to check a concierge doctor's board certification, Florida license and hospital privileges, and how to judge the harder part: whether the fit is right.

item.title: Telehealth with your own doctor: what works by video
item.description: Which visits work well by video with a doctor who already knows you, which ones still need the office, and how to get the most out of a video visit.

item.title: Why it helps when your internist is also a nephrologist
item.description: Kidneys, blood pressure, diabetes and medicines are closely linked. Here is why it helps to have one doctor trained in both internal medicine and nephrology.

item.title: Your annual physical: what the evidence says you need
item.description: What a yearly physical is for, which screenings the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends by age, and how Medicare's wellness visit differs.

item.title: A seasonal resident's guide to primary care in Palm Beach
item.description: Splitting the year between Palm Beach and home up north? How to keep one clear medical picture, a current medication list and a doctor who knows you.

item.title: How to move your medical records to a Florida doctor
item.description: A step-by-step guide to moving your medical records to a new doctor in Florida: what to ask for, your rights under HIPAA, fees, and timing.

item.title: Medicare when you live in two states
item.description: How Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage and Part D drug plans work when you split the year between Florida and another state, with dates to know.

item.title: A hurricane season health checklist for older adults
item.description: A practical hurricane checklist for older adults in Palm Beach County: medicines, records, power-dependent equipment, dialysis plans and family contacts.

item.title: Heat, hydration and your kidneys in South Florida
item.description: How heat and dehydration affect older adults and the kidneys in South Florida, which common medicines raise the risk, and when to call your doctor.

item.title: Concierge care for an aging parent: a guide for families
item.description: How families can coordinate a parent's care with one doctor: HIPAA permissions, a Florida health care surrogate, shared visits and a plan for calls.

item.title: Memory changes: what is normal, and when to see a doctor
item.description: How to tell normal forgetfulness from something more, what the National Institute on Aging says about treatable causes, and when to book a visit.

item.title: Too many medicines? Why a full medication review matters
item.description: Several doctors, several pharmacies, a shelf of supplements. Why older adults benefit from a full medication review, and what the Beers Criteria are.

item.title: eGFR, creatinine and UACR: reading your kidney labs
item.description: What eGFR, creatinine and the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio measure, what the ranges mean, and why one result is rarely the whole story.

item.title: How to check your blood pressure at home
item.description: How to choose a validated upper arm cuff, prepare, sit and record readings at home, following American Heart Association guidance, and what to share.
